newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says U.S. president won't "whip" him.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says U.S. president won't "whip" him.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday that the next president of the United States, whoever it might be, would not pressure him into peace concessions.

Asked during an interview on Israel's Channel One television if he thought Palestinian President Yasser Arafat hoped that after Tuesday's U.S. elections Washington would pressure Israel to compromise, Netanyahu said:
"First of all, if he is waiting for the great pressure that has to come from Washington, he will be disappointed because it will not come.
"The whole idea that Netanyahu will stand and be whipped by the next president of the United States is simply not serious."
The right-wing Netanyahu ousted Israel's previous centre-left government in May elections.

Netanyahu's government is currently in talks with the Palestine Liberation Organisation on implementing an accord signed by the previous government to redeploy Israeli troops in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Palestinians accuse Netanyahu of trying to change the signed deal. He says he wants to increase security for some 400 Jews who live and study in Hebron among 100,000 Palestinians.
President Bill Clinton all but openly endorsed former prime minister Shimon Peres over Netanyahu before Israel's elections.
Netanyahu said he was confident that whoever emerged the victor in the U.S. elections would maintain excellent ties with Israel -- and avoid interfering with it.

"I think that the relations are regular and good and friendly and based on a clear understanding that the one who has to decide on the fateful steps of the State of Israel is first of all the State of Israel and not the friend and partner on the other side of the ocean," he said.
Opinion polls in the run-up to the U.S. elections put Clinton ahead of Republican candidate Bob Dole.
